standard_prerequisites.name: Signed assumption set of a derivable sentence
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma proves A iff for some finite B_1,...,B_n in Gamma the set {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n} has a closed tableau.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis Gamma proves A is unpacked into a closed witness tableau whose first assumption is False A.

standard_prerequisites.name: The True-not rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: From the signed formula True (not A) the rule derives False A.
standard_prerequisites.use: The inserted line after the assumptions is the conclusion of the True-not rule, restoring the line the replaced assumption used to supply.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 962-965): if Gamma proves A and not A in Gamma, then Gamma is inconsistent.
Witness (proof lines 967-972): B_1,...,B_n in Gamma such that {False A, True B_1,...,True B_n} has a closed tableau.

Assumption replacement (proof lines 973-980): replace the assumption False A by True (not A) and insert the conclusion of the True-not rule applied to False A after the assumptions; every line justified by appeal to line 1 of the old tableau is justified by appeal to line n+1 of the new one, so closure carries over, and since all assumptions lie in Gamma the new tableau shows Gamma is inconsistent.
proof_roadmap: Unpack Gamma proves A into its closed witness tableau.
Swap the False A assumption for the in-Gamma True (not A) and reinsert False A as a derived line.
Renumber justifications and conclude closure of the new tableau.
difficulty_reason: Explicit inconsistency (statement 962-965, proof 967-981): the complete assumption-replacement and line-renumbering argument carried in span. H2.
